**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement affirmatively takes our preferred position:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013):** "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," Customer pays only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, and declining to enter another Order Form "is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 12.3 (p0051):** Confirms Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer or **minimum-volume** commitment.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026):** Bars Vendor from imposing any platform, support, administration or **minimum-use** charge not identified in the Order Form.

I also checked the planner's candidate sections: § 4 (Order Forms) has no committed quantities or non-reducible seat counts; § 7 has no take-or-pay or shortfall true-up; § 8.2 renews Order Forms only in twelve-month increments with a Customer-side thirty-day non-renewal right (plus a reminder-dependent extension), so there is no multi-year lock-in. The only "shortfall" references (§ 22.1–22.2) relate to Vendor's licence audit of actual usage, not a purchase commitment, and so do not engage this rule.

One item outside this rule's scope, flagged for the record: § 7.7 (p0032) imposes "liquidated damages" of 15% of *annual* Fees per week for late payment — an unenforceable-looking penalty on us that should be addressed under the late-payment/interest rule.
